summary: Steel Wisconsin DNR fire tower in Rusk County; a January 1983 sealed-bid notice is the only dated record found, and the FFLA lists it as gone.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association. No removal date or cause found in the sources read.

events.note: DNR invited sealed bids for the steel fire tower, described as about 100 feet tall.

evidence.supports: Ladd Creek is a fire tower in Sec 18, T36N, R3W, Rusk County
evidence.quote: Ladd Creek Fire Tower - Sec 18, T36N, R3W, Rusk Co.

evidence.supports: January 1983 sealed-bid notice by the State DNR, bids at Park Falls headquarters
evidence.quote: Sealed bids will be received by the State of Wisconsin, Department of Natural Resources at the Park Falls DNR Area Headquarter located at Park Falls, Wisconsin for a fire tower situated at the following location
Approximate height of the steel fire tower is 100 feet.

evidence.supports: Statewide lookouts manned May to September for many decades
evidence.quote: Manned from May to September for many decades, their staffing was reduced to the peak forest fire season, between snow melt and green up in the spring.

evidence.supports: 72 towers still in use were decommissioned in 2015 (statewide)
evidence.quote: In 2015, the 72 aging towers still in use were decommissioned.

evidence.supports: Listed as gone, at about 45.60 N, 90.80 W

sources.title: Connecting the dots: the fire towers of Wisconsin

notes_for_editor: Only one dated record: the 1983 bid notice, reprinted on Central US Lookouts as from The Capital Times. No construction date, staffing history, or removal record found. Height is the notice's approximate 100 ft converted to about 30 m. The Ladysmith News editorial on the 2015 phase-out returned HTTP 429 and was not read; the 2015 statewide figure comes from WJFW only. Ladd Creek is not tied to the 2015 decommissioning in any source read.
